'''Ahmed Amin Hamza''' <small>[[African Academy of Sciences|FAAS]] [[Royal Microscopical Society|FRMS]] [[International Society for Optical Engineering|SPIE]]</small> ({{Langx|ar|أحمد أمين حمزة}}) is an Egyptian emeritus professor of physics at the Faculty of Science, [[Mansoura University|University of Mansoura]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Hamza Ahmed Amin {{!}} The AAS |url=https://www.aasciences.africa/fellow/hamza-ahmed-amin |access-date=2022-06-26 |website=www.aasciences.africa |archive-date=2019-10-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191027133251/https://www.aasciences.africa/fellow/hamza-ahmed-amin |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Ahmed Amin Hamza - Board of Trustee Member at BUE University |url=https://theorg.com/org/bue-university/org-chart/ahmed-amin-hamza |access-date=2022-06-26 |website=THE ORG |language=en}}</ref> He was a former President  and Vice President of the institution and an ex-President of the [[The British University in Egypt|British University]] in [[Egypt]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />  He is a member of [[African Academy of Sciences]] and a fellow of the [[Institute of Physics|institute of physics]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

== Early life and education ==
Ahmed Amin Hamza was born on March 8, 1941.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Universities in Egypt |url=https://www.universitiesegypt.com/leadership.aspx?EId=562&WID=55 |access-date=2022-06-26 |website=www.universitiesegypt.com| date=17 September 2015 }}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Prof. Ahmed Amin Hamza |url=http://staff.mans.edu.eg/hamzaaa/english/ |access-date=2022-06-26 |website=staff.mans.edu.eg}}</ref>
He obtained his first degree, B. Sc Physics and Chemistry,  from [[Ain Shams University]], [[Cairo]]  in 1962 with Honors. In 1964 and 1967, he received a diploma degree in Optical Metrology and M. Sc in Physics respectively. In 1972, he obtained his PhD in physics from the same institution .<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":0" />

== Career ==
After his first degree, he was appointed as the head of Colour-section, Cairo Dyeing and Finishing Company, Cairo in 1962. A year after his M. Sc, he became the Head of Printing Department of the same company. In 1972, he became a lecturer of Physics at the Faculty of Science in University of Mansoura, Egypt. In 1976, he became as assistant Professor, in 1981, he became professor of Experimental Physics and in 2001, he became an emeritus professor in the same Institution.<ref name=":2" />

== Administrative appointments ==
He was the Head of Physics Department, Faculty of Science, [[Mansoura University|University of Mansoura]] from 1984 - 1986 and the Vice Dean of the Faculty of Science from 1986 - 1992.<ref name=":2" /> He was the Vice President for Community and Environmental Development, University of Mansoura for two years; August 1992 - August, 1994.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" /> He became the President of the University of Mansoura on August 5, 1994 and left the position in July 31, 2001.<ref>{{cite web |title=History - Mansura University |url=https://www.mans.edu.eg/en/about/history-and-facts/history |access-date=24 August 2026}}</ref> From 2005 to 2008, he was the vice President of [[The British University in Egypt|British University in Egypt]] and In 2008, he became the  President of the same institution; a position that he left in 2013.<ref name=":2" />

== Memberships and fellowships ==
In 1977, he became a Fellow of the [[Royal Microscopical Society]], FRMS in [[Oxford]] and in 1982, he became a Fellow of the [[Institute of Physics]] in [[London]].<ref name=":2" /> He became part of [[International Society for Optical Engineering]] SPIE in 1989 and in 1995, he became a Member of the [[New York Academy of Sciences]].<ref name=":2" /> In the same year, he became a Member of the Egyptian Academy of Sciences, [[African Academy of Sciences]] and [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]<ref name=":2" />

== Award ==
In 1987, he received the Egyptian National Award in Physics and in 1992, he was awarded University of Mansoura Award of Merit. In 1995, he received Egyptian President distinguished merit award and in the same year, he received the Scientists Certificate of Merit from the Academy of Scientific Research & Technology, and the Egyptian Syndicate of Scientific Professions. In 1997,  the State Prize of Merit in Basic Science, three years later, he received [[Honorary degree|Doctor honoris causa]] (Dr.h.c) from the [[Technical University of Liberec]], Czeck Republic. In 2005, he received the  El-Nile "Mubarak" Prize in Advanced Technological Science, The highest National award in Egypt.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":0" />
